title: Orsen and the Vow
premise: Marine biologist Yara Sandoval has spent a decade hiding from a betrayal that cost her family everything, counting sea turtles instead of confronting the man she once loved. When a community outreach program anonymously pairs her with a pen pal, the letters grow into the most honest relationship of her life—until she discovers her correspondent is Orsen Vale, the whistleblower whose testimony destroyed her father and whose own vow of silence was bought at a terrible price. Forced to work together to save the nesting beach both of them love, Yara must choose between loyalty to her family's grief and the truth she's spent ten years avoiding: that Orsen lied to survive, just as she did. In the end, she forgives him only after forgiving herself, and the final letter is signed with both their names.
about_author: P. M. Galloway is the pen name of a former coastal field researcher who traded tide charts for typewriters after a decade of studying what survives in hostile waters. Galloway writes quiet, salt-stained romances about people who mistake endurance for peace.

chapters.title: The Counting Season
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On Isla Verde, Yara logs the season's first turtle nests, her careful routines a fortress against the past. A letter arrives announcing the town's anonymous pen-pal program—a fundraiser she can't refuse without drawing attention. Emotional beat: the comfort of control, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: Dear Stranger
chapters.summary: Yara and Orsen's alternating letters. She writes guarded, witty prose about turtles; her correspondent answers with startling honesty about regret. Orsen, we learn in his POV, joined the program on a dare from his sister. Emotional beat: two people practicing intimacy they believe is safe because it's anonymous.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A flashback braided into the present: ten years ago, her father's fishing cooperative collapsed after an anonymous testimony exposed illegal permits—testimony signed by Orsen Vale, her then-fiancé's best friend and her own first love. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into a weapon she still carries.

chapters.title: The Man in the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen lives alone in the decommissioned lighthouse, keeping the island's weather log and his own vow of silence about who pressured him to testify. He recognizes Yara's handwriting from an old letter she once wrote him and realizes who his pen pal is. Emotional beat: terror and longing in equal measure.

chapters.title: Erosion
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The nesting beach is eroding faster than the season's models predict; a resort developer's seawall proposal would doom it. The town council assigns Yara and the lighthouse keeper—Orsen—to co-author the counterproposal. Emotional beat: dread disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Letters We Shouldn't Answer
chapters.summary: Alternating letters and work scenes. Yara tells her pen pal about her 'impossible' new colleague; Orsen tells his that he's falling for someone who would hate him if she knew his name. Emotional beat: the delicious, doomed irony of confiding the secret in the person it's kept from.

chapters.title: Nest at High Tide
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Working nights relocating a threatened nest, Yara and Orsen fall into rhythm—her expertise, his weather knowledge, old shorthand returning unbidden. She catches herself laughing and hates it. Emotional beat: the body remembering what the mind has forbidden.

chapters.title: The Vow
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Full flashback: nineteen-year-old Orsen, drowning in his family's debt, was coerced by the developer's lawyer into testifying against the cooperative—and against Yara's father specifically. He swore never to speak the name of who held the leverage. Emotional beat: shame as a life sentence.

chapters.title: Small Safe Steps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Her mother visits, pressing her to finally date the dependable harbormaster, Mateo. Yara realizes her decade of small safe steps was never recovery—it was retreat. That night she writes her pen pal the most honest letter yet. Emotional beat: the ache of a life half-lived.

chapters.title: Storm Log
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A tropical storm strands them in the lighthouse; the counterproposal drafts soak through, and they rebuild them by lantern light. Orsen nearly tells her everything, twice. Yara, half-asleep against his shoulder, murmurs that she wishes her pen pal were real. Emotional beat: proximity as confession.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Reviewing archived testimony for the counterproposal, Yara recognizes a phrase in Orsen's formal statement—the same phrase from his letters. She cross-checks the pen-pal envelopes. The handwriting matches. Emotional beat: the floor giving way.

chapters.title: What I Would Have Said
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen senses her withdrawal at work but not its cause; he writes his pen pal asking how to tell someone the truth when it will cost you everything, including them. Yara reads the letter and doesn't answer. Emotional beat: two people talking past each other in the same room.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Seawall
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the developer's public hearing, Yara watches Orsen argue passionately against the seawall—and detonates afterward, confronting him on the beach: the testimony, the letters, the lie of the last months. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal, truth as a blade used badly.

chapters.title: The Leverage
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Cornered, Orsen breaks his vow and tells Yara why he testified: the lawyer held evidence that would have imprisoned her father for a far worse offense—and her father begged Orsen to take the deal. Emotional beat: the revelation that reframes a decade of hatred.

chapters.title: My Father's Hands
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Shattered, Yara confronts her father, who confirms it—and asks her to keep the secret, as he has, to protect the family. She realizes she's being asked to make Orsen's choice all over again. Emotional beat: loyalty and truth tearing in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Empty Desk
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Orsen resigns from the counterproposal and prepares to leave the island, believing he's finally repaid his debt by losing the thing he loves. He leaves his final letter unmailed. Emotional beat: self-erasure mistaken for atonement.

chapters.title: Reading the Unsent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara finds the unsent letter in the lighthouse—ten pages of the truth, ending with the sentence he could never say aloud. She reads her father's old letters too and sees, for the first time, her own decade of silence as its own kind of lie. Emotional beat: forgiveness of the man in the mirror.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the final council vote, Yara takes the floor and tells the whole story—her father's crime, Orsen's coerced silence, her own decade of hiding—risking everything to save the beach. The town, and her father, must sit with the truth. Emotional beat: truth chosen over loyalty, publicly and at cost.

chapters.title: The Vote and the Storm
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The council rejects the seawall, but a storm surge hits that night; the relocated nests are threatened. Orsen returns to help, and he and Yara work the water side by side, past grievance, into partnership. Emotional beat: the climax—nature's crisis mirroring the emotional one, and both survived together.

chapters.title: Hatchlings
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At dawn, the hatchlings make their run to the sea while the town watches—her father among them, having come to stand beside her, his secret now a shared weight rather than a wall. Yara and Orsen stand at the tideline, not touching, everything changed. Emotional beat: quiet, earned tenderness.

chapters.title: The Last Assignment
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The pen-pal program announces a new season; Orsen submits one letter, addressed to Yara by name for the first time, asking for a second chance with nothing hidden. She answers in person at the lighthouse door. Emotional beat: the vow rewritten—not silence, but honesty.

chapters.title: Both Our Names
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, epilogue. A year later: the beach is protected, the counterproposal published under both their names, and a new letter arrives for the season's pen-pal program—already answered, because they no longer need strangers to say true things. Yara counts turtles, and for once, counts herself among the things that survived. Emotional beat: belonging, chosen and kept.
